asvs_target.baseline: ASVS L2 (all applicable L1 + L2 requirements are in scope)
asvs_target.rationale: Wallet authentication, contract-wallet (Safe) authority, Telegram account binding and financial-protection workflows justify L2 everywhere and L3 only where the threat model has a concrete path (nonce strength, TOCTOU/locking, re-authentication for sensitive operations, embedding, data minimisation/retention, immediate authorisation changes, multi-party approval). Fixed in Phase 1 before evidence review; unchanged in 1B.

release_classes.RELEASE_BLOCKING: FAIL or insufficient evidence blocks release
release_classes.SECURITY_DEBT: tracked; FAIL stays FAIL; does not block release by itself
release_classes.MANUAL_ASSURANCE: property verified by dated human/platform record; automation pending
release_classes.INFORMATIONAL: documented constraint/assumption; FAIL stays FAIL and visible

combination_rule: Complementary evidence may be combined ACROSS sub-properties (each sub-property needs its own satisfying evidence). Within one sub-property, a cover marked PARTIAL never satisfies it.
acceptance_rules: Evidence must be reproducible from the repository at the verified commit; non-reproducible evidence only satisfies MANUAL_ASSURANCE / automation NO controls, and only if it is a dated manual record.
E4 requires a reproducible known-bad/mutation proof with result KILLED for the property.
Comments in code/tests are never evidence; source-text and config-text checks are E1.
A test that survives a known-bad variant is invalid evidence (known_bad_result SURVIVED -> ignored).
FAIL arises only from an evidence finding VIOLATION; it can only disappear with an entry in classification-changes.json.
E6 is not claimed: no independent external review exists.
Executable evidence counts only if it was executed in this run and passed; evidence that could not run (missing environment) counts as missing, never as passed.

Mutation (known-bad) evidence counts for a property only if at least one case targeting it was KILLED by its expected failing test with behavioural detection, and no case targeting it SURVIVED, was killed for another reason, was invalid, or did not run in this run. EQUIVALENT cases are neutral.
A declared mutation result that differs from the observed result invalidates the framework run.
An evidence item may not declare a level above the cap of its type (evidence_level_cap_by_type); E5 therefore requires real-system evidence.

STRUCTURAL evidence satisfies only the properties listed in structural_property_rule.allowed (each also marked evidence_basis STRUCTURAL in its control), only as executable static evidence naming a standard-library primitive at an exact call site with client_selectable false; it is reported as structurally verified, not mutation-proven, and never applies to any other property.

status_axes.conformance_status: Does the implementation meet the literal external (or CRSF-internal) requirement? CONFORMANT | NON_CONFORMANT | NOT_DEMONSTRATED | ACCEPTED_PROTOCOL_DEVIATION | ACCEPTED_PLATFORM_DEVIATION | NOT_APPLICABLE | DEFERRED. NOT_DEMONSTRATED is a Phase-1C extension: without evidence neither CONFORMANT nor NON_CONFORMANT can be asserted.
status_axes.security_status: Is the security property demonstrated? PASS_AUTOMATED | PASS_MANUAL | MISSING_EVIDENCE | FAIL | INFORMATIONAL | NOT_APPLICABLE | DEFERRED. INFORMATIONAL only for a validated accepted deviation whose remaining security properties are all satisfied and no defect exists.
status_axes.never_combined: The two axes are never merged into one score; a deviation is never reported as PASS.

property_kinds.REQUIREMENT: literal requirement that is also the security property (default); violation => FAIL and NON_CONFORMANT
property_kinds.CONFORMANCE: literal standard text that may be the subject of a deviation; violation => NON_CONFORMANT and FAIL unless an ACCEPTED, validated deviation covers exactly this property
property_kinds.SECURITY: CRSF-defined assurance property that must hold regardless of any deviation; violation => FAIL

PROTOCOL: A pinned external protocol directly or unavoidably requires the differing behaviour
B CoverRaccoon needs that protocol for intended functionality
C no standards-conformant alternative without losing required protocol compatibility
D narrow: exactly one external requirement and only CONFORMANCE properties
E no independent implementation defect (checked: listed implementation controls are not FAIL)
F the protocol is mature/authoritative (Final status or formal/reference specification)
G documented: standard reference, conflicting requirement, protocol requirement, reason, threat analysis, mitigation, review triggers
PLATFORM: PD2 no application-level configurable secure alternative
E no independent implementation defect (as PROTOCOL)

deviation_rules.status: computed: any criterion not met => REJECTED; all met but a machine check fails => REQUIRES_REVIEW; otherwise ACCEPTED. Only ACCEPTED deviations affect any status.
forbidden: deviation without a VIOLATION finding on the deviated property
deviation on a REQUIREMENT or SECURITY property
deviation whose sources are not pinned
one deviation spanning several external requirements
deviation hiding a FAIL of an implementation control
deviation_rules.owner_signoff: PENDING until the repository owner reviews the record; APPROVED requires owner_signoff_record {by, date, reference}. Tooling never sets APPROVED.

mutation_rules.workspace: disposable copy of tracked + untracked non-ignored files; node_modules symlinked; deleted afterwards; the working tree is never modified
mutation_rules.edits: exact text anchors that must occur exactly once
mutation_rules.baseline: the unmutated workspace must pass every mapped test first, otherwise no case is evaluated
mutation_rules.detection: behavioral kills count for E4; static (source-text) kills are recorded but never count
mutation_rules.equivalence: EQUIVALENT requires a written proof (kind UNREACHABLE or REDUNDANT_LAYER). It never counts as E4 and never as SURVIVED, stays visible in every report, and becomes a claim violation if any mapped test kills it.
mutation_rules.multi_layer: MULTI_LAYER: several edits that together form ONE logical defect across deliberately redundant checks; needs >= 2 edits and a written rationale. A single redundant layer removal is EQUIVALENT (REDUNDANT_LAYER), never a SURVIVED security failure.

verify_policy.evidence_failure: exit 1 (an executed security test failed, was cancelled, todo, or skipped unexpectedly)
verify_policy.release_assertion_rule: RELEASE_SECURITY_ASSERTION is PASS only if every RELEASE_BLOCKING control is PASS_AUTOMATED in the observed run; any RELEASE_BLOCKING FAIL => FAIL; otherwise INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE

structural_property_rule.statement: Owner decision (Phase 2D): two implementation invariants of CR-SESSION-001 may be satisfied by STRUCTURAL evidence because constant-time behaviour and algorithm fixation are not reliably observable by black-box mutation in JavaScript. Such evidence is static, executable (re-checked every run against the exact call site), names a Node standard-library primitive and records that no client input selects or replaces it. Properties met this way are reported as structurally verified, never as behaviourally mutation-proven. The allowlist is exhaustive; any other property marked STRUCTURAL is a framework error.
